title: Felix and the Asset
premise: Isandro Kavanagh, a private security contractor who keeps her clients' secrets and her own, is approached by a stranger named Felix who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of doing. The debt he repays drags her into the orbit of Meridian Group, the deniable-operations firm that trained her and erased the record of it. As Felix's evidence mounts, Isandro realizes her missing memories hold the key to a ledger of assassinations disguised as 'extractions,' and that Meridian will burn anyone who remembers. Hunted by her own former handlers and unsure whether Felix is savior or bait, she must choose between loyalty to the people who made her and the truth of what they made her do. In the end she torches Meridian's network from inside its own safehouse, puts the ledger in the hands of a journalist, and boards the dawn extraction flight alone — alive, disavowed, and finally free.
about_author: S. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients who preferred to remain unnamed. They now write fiction from a coastal town whose location they decline to confirm.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Between contracts in Lisbon, a soft-spoken stranger named Felix intercepts her, thanking her for pulling him out of a fire in Sarajevo — an operation she has no record of. He leaves a burner phone and a warning: interest is owed. Beat: unease dressed as flattery.

chapters.title: Retainer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She runs Felix's name through every database she trusts and finds him scrubbed — professionally, recently. Her old handler, Voss, calls with a routine audit request that feels anything but. Beat: the first cold drop of being watched.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He explains the debt: Meridian Group, the contractor that trained them both, used a Sarajevo extraction as cover for a murder, and Isandro was the unwitting witness. He offers proof — if she helps him reach it. Beat: reluctant alliance over mutual distrust.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She breaks into her own archived personnel file at a Meridian data vault and finds a six-month gap where her memory should be. Someone paid to have it sealed. Beat: vertigo — the self she trusted has holes in it.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He reveals half of a coded ledger linking twelve 'extractions' to political deaths across three continents. The other half sits in Meridian's Geneva safehouse, behind biometrics only alumni can pass. Beat: the scale of it lands like a weight.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Under orders to assess Isandro's loyalty, Voss struggles between fatherly protectiveness and institutional obedience. He warns her off with a story about what happened to the last alumnus who asked questions. Beat: love weaponized as a leash.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She and Felix rehearse the Geneva infiltration in a derelict farmhouse, trading tradecraft and life stories. A tail appears on the road; they barely slip it. Beat: trust forming under pressure, fragile as glass.

chapters.title: The Alumni Network
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She contacts Mara, a fellow alumna turned fixer, who confirms the memory gap is standard practice — 'hygiene.' Mara refuses to help but slips her a Geneva access code anyway. Beat: solidarity among the erased.

chapters.title: Geneva
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The infiltration goes clean until the biometric door logs Isandro's retina and triggers a silent alarm neither anticipated. They get the ledger half out as the building locks down around them. Beat: triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. By morning she is officially rogue: accounts frozen, face circulated, a kill-on-sight order quietly issued. She realizes the alarm wasn't a malfunction — someone wanted her flushed into the open. Beat: betrayal sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Isandro confronts Felix: was she recruited or harvested? He admits Meridian let him find her, betting she'd lead them to the ledger's second key — which, he confesses, isn't a document. It's her sealed memory. Beat: the alliance cracks down to its studs.

chapters.title: Mara's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara agrees to hide them in exchange for deletion from the alumni rolls — a favor Meridian grants no one. While forging the paperwork she uncovers the flight manifest for a dawn extraction out of a private airfield. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Hygiene
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A Meridian retrieval team corners them; Felix takes a bullet covering her escape. In the aftermath, a captured team member confirms the truth: the Sarajevo fire, the erased months, all of it scripted to build an operator with no conscience left to interrogate. Beat: grief fused to fury.

chapters.title: What the Gap Contains
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Under Mara's guidance, Isandro begins recovering fragments: faces, a name — Director Hale — and the moment she signed away the memory herself, believing she was protecting a colleague. Beat: horror at complicity, not just victimhood.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The director who built Meridian's hygiene program reviews Isandro's file like a proud parent reading a disappointing child's report card. He authorizes the dawn flight not as escape but as disposal, mid-air. Beat: banal, paternal evil.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, convalescing. Felix brokers a meet with investigative journalist Odile Ferrand, who can authenticate the ledger but needs the second key — Isandro's testimony — within thirty-six hours or the story dies legally. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro chooses testimony over safety, dictating her recovered memories while Mara scrubs traces of their route. Voss calls one last time, begging her to board the flight and let it go. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth choice made explicit, then refused.

chapters.title: The Airfield Gambit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Instead of fleeing the airfield, Isandro walks onto it — boarding the extraction flight carrying a device that will broadcast the ledger to every newsroom and regulator on Ferrand's list the moment wheels lift. Beat: turning Meridian's own machinery against itself.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Climax, Isandro's POV. Mid-flight, the broadcast fires. Hale's people scramble to force a landing; Isandro fights her way to the cockpit, forces a diversion, and walks off the tarmac as the ledger detonates across the world's screens behind her. Beat: catharsis at terminal velocity.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Hale is detained by his own board; Voss resigns rather than testify against Isandro; alumni worldwide begin coming forward. Ferrand's series breaks. Beat: the network burning exactly as promised, from the inside out.

chapters.title: Debrief
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro and Felix, both healing, meet one last time in Lisbon. Neither thanks the other; both understand the debt is settled. She declines his offer of partnership — some debts should end, not continue. Beat: quiet, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Disavowed, unemployable, and lighter than she's ever been, Isandro boards a commercial flight at dawn under her own name for the first time in years. No client, no handler, no gap in the record. Beat: freedom as an ending, not a reward.
